thread.title: Bear trapped inside car near California-Nevada border destroys interior, leaves destructed auto
thread.title_full: Bear trapped inside car near California-Nevada border destroys interior, leaves destructed auto

author: Golden Gate Media
title: Bear trapped inside car near California-Nevada border destroys interior, leaves destructed auto
text:
11 hours ago A routine call in Incline Village quickly turned into a startling wildlife encounter when deputies with the Washoe County Sheriff's Office arrived to find a bear trapped inside a vehicle. According to the sheriff’s office, the situation unfolded when the vehicle’s owner opened the door and came face-to-face with the unexpected intruder.
Photo by Washoe County Sheriff “A call in Incline brought our patrol deputies to quite the scene after a vehicle owner opened their car door and discovered an unexpected visitor inside, a bear that had become trapped in the vehicle,” the agency said in a statement. The encounter ended as abruptly as it began. “The bear quickly ran off once the door was opened, leaving behind significant damage.”
The incident underscores a growing seasonal pattern across the Lake Tahoe Basin, where bear activity typically ramps up in spring. As temperatures rise and natural food sources shift, bears are increasingly drawn to residential areas in search of easy meals, often targeting unsecured vehicles and trash.
Authorities are urging residents and visitors to take precautions to avoid dangerous encounters. The sheriff’s office emphasized the importance of keeping vehicles free of food and scented items, ensuring doors and windows are secured, and properly storing outdoor cooking equipment. Trash should always be disposed of in bear-proof containers, and officials stress that feeding bears is strictly discouraged.
“Help keep our wildlife wild for your safety and theirs,” the agency said, reinforcing a message that echoes across mountain communities during peak bear season.
